subject.title: Add an auditable native ShellBench matrix runner

question: Should ShellBench adopt a first-party native Crabbox matrix runner and Harbor-gated leaderboard eligibility, and if so which minimum audit and calibration contract should be the initial milestone?
rationale: This changes benchmark operations and leaderboard policy across several subsystems; source-level repair work cannot safely choose the product boundary, cost model, retention policy, or calibration threshold.

options.title: Sponsor a staged native runner
options.body: Define a small first milestone around one matrix, durable evidence artifacts, and an explicit Harbor parity gate before expanding fleet and leaderboard coverage.

options.title: Keep native execution external
options.body: Document an external runner or integration contract and retain Harbor as the only first-party leaderboard route for now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged native runner
recommendation.body: Define a small first milestone around one matrix, durable evidence artifacts, and an explicit Harbor parity gate before expanding fleet and leaderboard coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The member author provided the proposed operational model and is the only evidenced routing candidate in the supplied context.
